stories.headline: Tens of thousands protest in Prague against Babiš government over defense cuts and democracy concerns
stories.summary: Czech Republic's largest anti-government demonstration since 2019 drew tens of thousands to Prague's Letná park on March 21, with protesters condemning PM Babiš for defense spending cuts and alleged democratic backsliding. Organizers from Million Moments for Democracy accused the government of steering toward autocracy.

stories.headline: Fire at Czech arms facility investigated as terrorism, prompts Babiš to cancel CPAC trip
stories.summary: A warehouse fire at LPP Holding's drone manufacturing facility in Pardubice on March 20 is being investigated as suspected terrorism after an anti-Israel group claimed responsibility. The incident prompted PM Babiš to cancel his planned CPAC appearance in Budapest and convene the National Security Council.

stories.headline: President Pavel visits Central Bohemia, criticizes government defense spending
stories.summary: President Petr Pavel conducted a two-day visit to Central Bohemia region March 18-19, meeting with mayors, visiting Škoda Auto, and holding public discussions in Nymburk. He used the visits to criticize the government's insufficient defense spending and express concerns about NATO commitments.

stories.headline: Czech defense spending cuts draw US and NATO criticism
stories.summary: Czech President Pavel and US NATO Ambassador Matthew Whitaker criticized the Babiš government's 2026 budget for inadequate defense spending, with the US warning that Czech defense outlays may fall short of NATO's 2% GDP commitment. The government defended its spending as compliant but faces pressure from allies.

stories.headline: Babiš announces he will attend NATO summit instead of President Pavel
stories.summary: PM Babiš told Czech Television he plans to attend the July NATO summit in Ankara instead of President Pavel, breaking with traditional practice. Babiš said he could better explain Czech defense spending decisions, while Pavel expressed surprise at not being consulted about the change.

stories.headline: Czech fuel prices rise due to Middle East conflict
stories.summary: Diesel and gasoline prices in Czech Republic reached multi-year highs following escalation in the Middle East conflict between Israel/US and Iran. Government officials discussed potential measures to cap fuel prices if they exceed regional levels.
